learn.hook: How much lace goes around a dupatta? How long is the boundary rope of a cricket ground? That's perimeter!
points: Perimeter is the total distance around the boundary of a shape. Add the lengths of all the sides.
Rectangle: perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth).
Square: perimeter = 4 × side.
Regular polygon (all sides equal): perimeter = number of sides × side length. An equilateral triangle is 3 × side.
Perimeter is a length, so it uses units like cm or m.

example.q: A garden is 12 m long and 8 m wide. How much fencing goes all round it?

learn.reallife: Framing a photo, putting lights around a window for Diwali and running laps of a ground all use perimeter.

items.q: Side of a square with perimeter 36 cm
Triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm, 5 cm

games.title: Match the shape to its perimeter

quiz.q: Riya's rangoli is a square of side 15 cm. She sticks ribbon all around its edge. How much ribbon does she need?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 equal sides, so the perimeter is 4 × 15 = 60 cm.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies side × side (area, 225) or uses only 2 or 3 sides

quiz.q: The boundary rope of a school cricket ground goes around a rectangle 70 m long and 50 m wide. How long is the rope?
quiz.mistake: Adds length and breadth only once (120) or multiplies them (area)

quiz.q: Arjun walks 3 times around a triangular park with sides 30 m, 40 m and 50 m. How far does he walk?
quiz.explain: One round is 30 + 40 + 50 = 120 m. Three rounds are 3 × 120 = 360 m.
quiz.mistake: Gives the distance for only one round (120 m)

quiz.q: The perimeter of a square is 48 cm. How long is one side?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 equal sides, so one side = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 2 instead of 4 (24) or multiplies (192)

quiz.q: A rectangle has perimeter 30 cm and length 10 cm. What is its breadth?
quiz.explain: Half the perimeter is length + breadth = 15 cm. So breadth = 15 − 10 = 5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 10 from 30 without halving first (20)

quiz.q: A regular hexagon tile has each side 8 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: A hexagon has 6 equal sides: 6 × 8 = 48 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the wrong number of sides (5, 7 or 8)

quiz.q: Which has the bigger perimeter: a square of side 6 cm or a rectangle 8 cm by 3 cm?
quiz.explain: Square: 4 × 6 = 24 cm. Rectangle: 2 × (8 + 3) = 22 cm. The square is bigger.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the shape with the longest side must have the bigger perimeter

quiz.q: Fencing costs ₹5 per metre. How much does it cost to fence a plot 20 m long and 10 m wide?
quiz.mistake: Uses area (200 × 5 = ₹1000) or forgets to multiply by the rate (₹60)

teach.ask: Gappu wants to put twigs all around his nest: 'How do I find the perimeter?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Walk around the edge and add every side. Now I know how many twigs I need!
teach.nudge: What do I do with the lengths of the sides? And is it inside or around the shape?

learn.hook: Round and round the track: after 1 km, where exactly are you standing?
points: Distance covered on a track = number of rounds × perimeter. 5 rounds of a 400 m track is 2000 m = 2 km.
To find where you stop: take away full rounds, then walk the leftover distance side by side from the start.
Bending a wire into a new shape keeps its length, so the perimeter stays the same. A wire square of side 12 cm (48 cm) can be bent into an equilateral triangle of side 48 ÷ 3 = 16 cm.
For curvy or irregular shapes, first estimate the perimeter, then check by laying a thread along the edge and measuring the thread.

example.q: A square park has side 50 m. Kavya starts at corner A and walks 325 m along the edge. Where is she?
steps: 125 m = 2 sides (100 m) + 25 m. She is 25 m along the third side from A.

learn.reallife: Athletes run laps on a 400 m track, and electricians bend wires into frames for lamps.

items.q: Rounds of a 400 m track to run 2 km
Distance in 3 rounds of a 250 m park
Wire square of side 9 cm bent into a triangle: side
Wire rectangle 7 by 5 bent into a square: side

games.title: Track and wire facts
items: Bending a wire into a new shape changes its length.
The wire's length stays the same.
6 rounds of a 200 m field is 1.2 km.
A thread can help measure the perimeter of a leaf.
Lay it along the edge and measure it.
A wire triangle of side 10 cm can be bent into a square of side 7.5 cm.
A good estimate must be exactly right.
An estimate is close, then we check by measuring.

quiz.q: Sunil runs 7 rounds of a rectangular field 80 m by 40 m. How far does he run?
quiz.mistake: Uses only length + breadth for one round

quiz.q: How many rounds of a 250 m track make 2 km?
quiz.mistake: Forgets 1 km = 1000 m

quiz.q: A square garden has side 30 m. Asif starts at a corner and walks 200 m along the edge. How far is he along the side he ends on?
quiz.explain: One round is 120 m. 200 − 120 = 80 m = 2 sides (60 m) + 20 m.
quiz.mistake: Stops after one round

quiz.q: A wire is bent into a rectangle 15 cm by 9 cm. It is then bent into a square. What is the side of the square?
quiz.explain: Wire length = 2 × (15 + 9) = 48 cm. Square side = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 2 instead of 4

quiz.q: A wire square of side 15 cm is reshaped into an equilateral triangle. What is each side?
quiz.explain: Wire = 4 × 15 = 60 cm. Triangle side = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 cm.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the same side length

quiz.q: Roshni lays a thread round a leaf and the thread measures 23 cm. What is the leaf's perimeter?
quiz.explain: The thread follows the boundary, so its length is the perimeter.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the thread length

quiz.q: Two friends run: Manu does 3 rounds of a 400 m track, Tanu does 5 rounds of a 250 m track. Who runs further and by how much?
quiz.explain: Manu: 3 × 400 = 1200 m. Tanu: 5 × 250 = 1250 m. Tanu runs 50 m more.
quiz.mistake: Compares rounds instead of distance

quiz.q: Which is the best way to estimate the perimeter of a curved pond drawn on a map?
options: Estimate, then check with a thread placed along the edge
quiz.explain: Estimate first, then a thread along the curve gives a good check.
quiz.mistake: Confuses perimeter with area

teach.ask: Gappu bends a 24 cm wire from a square into a triangle. 'Which shape uses more wire?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Same wire, same length: both have perimeter 24 cm!
teach.nudge: Does the wire get longer or shorter when bent?

topics.title: Perimeter puzzles: two units and rearranging

learn.hook: Cut a shape and move the pieces: the area stays, but the perimeter can change. Surprise!
points: On a dot grid, edges can be straight units (along the grid) or diagonal units (corner to corner of a square). A diagonal unit is longer than a straight unit.
Write such a perimeter as, for example, '4 straight + 2 diagonal units'. Don't add them as if they were the same length.
Split and rejoin: cutting a shape into pieces and joining them in a new way keeps the area, but the perimeter may go up or down.
A 6 cm × 2 cm strip (perimeter 16 cm) cut in half and stacked into a 3 cm × 4 cm rectangle has perimeter 14 cm. The area is 12 cm² both times.
Puzzles like Matha Pachchi ask you to fit the same pieces into different shapes and compare their perimeters: same area, different boundaries.

example.q: A 8 cm × 2 cm strip is cut into two 4 cm × 2 cm pieces, which are placed side by side along their 4 cm sides to make a square. Compare perimeters.
steps: Two 4 × 2 pieces joined along 4 cm make a 4 cm × 4 cm square: 4 × 4 = 16 cm.
Area stays 16 cm², but the perimeter drops by 4 cm.

learn.reallife: Tailors cut and rearrange cloth pieces; the cloth (area) is the same, but the length of edging needed can change.

games.title: Rearranging pieces
items: Cutting and rearranging pieces keeps the area the same.
No cloth is added or lost.
Cutting and rearranging always keeps the perimeter the same.
The perimeter can change.
A diagonal unit is the same length as a straight unit.
The diagonal is longer.
2 straight + 2 diagonal units cannot be written as 4 units.
The two kinds have different lengths.
A long thin shape has a bigger perimeter than a compact shape of the same area.
More of its edge is exposed.

games.title: Smallest to largest perimeter
items: 4 cm × 4 cm
8 cm × 2 cm
16 cm × 1 cm

quiz.q: A 10 cm × 2 cm strip is cut into two 5 cm × 2 cm pieces and stacked to make a 5 cm × 4 cm rectangle. What is the new perimeter?
quiz.explain: New rectangle: 2 × (5 + 4) = 18 cm. (The strip had 24 cm.)
quiz.mistake: Assumes the perimeter stays the same

quiz.q: In that rearrangement (10 × 2 strip → 5 × 4 rectangle), what happens to the area?
quiz.explain: The same paper is used, so the area stays 10 × 2 = 20 cm².
quiz.mistake: Thinks area changes with shape

quiz.q: A shape on a dot grid has 6 straight units and 2 diagonal units round its edge. Which is the correct way to write its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Diagonal and straight units are different lengths, so we keep them separate.
quiz.mistake: Adds two different kinds of unit

quiz.q: Which is longer: 4 straight units or 4 diagonal units?
quiz.explain: Each diagonal unit is longer than a straight unit, so 4 diagonals are longer.
quiz.mistake: Thinks units with the same count are equal

quiz.q: A 12 cm × 1 cm strip is cut into three 4 cm × 1 cm pieces placed side by side along their long sides (forming 4 cm × 3 cm). What is the new perimeter?
quiz.explain: 2 × (4 + 3) = 14 cm, down from 26 cm.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the old perimeter

quiz.q: Two 3 cm × 3 cm squares are joined edge to edge. What is the perimeter of the new shape?
quiz.explain: It is a 6 cm × 3 cm rectangle: 2 × (6 + 3) = 18 cm. The joined edges are inside.
quiz.mistake: Adds both squares' perimeters (24 cm)

quiz.q: In a pieces puzzle, Lata makes a square and then a long rectangle using all the same pieces. Which is true?
options: The square has a bigger area
The rectangle has a smaller perimeter
quiz.explain: The same pieces cover the same area. The long shape usually has a bigger perimeter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks same pieces give the same perimeter

quiz.q: A square of side 4 cm is cut along a line into two 4 cm × 2 cm rectangles, which are put end to end to make an 8 cm × 2 cm strip. By how much does the perimeter change?
quiz.explain: Square: 16 cm. Strip: 2 × (8 + 2) = 20 cm. 20 − 16 = 4 cm more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rearranging never changes perimeter

teach.ask: Gappu cuts his square leaf into two strips and lines them up end to end. 'Did my leaf get bigger?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Same area, but the edge (perimeter) got longer!
teach.nudge: Did you add any leaf? What happened to the edge?

learn.hook: How many tiles will cover your classroom floor? Area tells you how much surface a shape covers.
points: Area is the amount of surface a shape covers. We measure it in square units like cm² and m².
Count the unit squares inside, or use a rule: area of a rectangle = length × breadth.
Area of a square = side × side.
Use the same unit for both sides: don't multiply cm by m.
Area and perimeter are different: two shapes can have the same area but different perimeters.

example.q: A floor is 5 m long and 4 m wide. How many 1 m × 1 m tiles cover it?

learn.reallife: Buying a carpet, painting a wall or planting grass on a lawn all depend on area.

items.text: A rectangle 9 cm × 4 cm has area ___ cm²
A square of side 7 m has area ___ m²
Area 40 cm² and length 8 cm, so breadth = ___ cm
A square of area 64 cm² has side ___ cm

games.title: Perimeter or area?
items: Lace around a tablecloth
Fence around a farm
Frame around a photo
Boundary rope of a cricket field
Carpet to cover a floor
Paint for a wall
Grass to cover a lawn
Tiles for a kitchen floor

quiz.q: Kabir's notebook cover is 20 cm long and 15 cm wide. What is its area?
quiz.explain: Area = length × breadth = 20 × 15 = 300 cm².
quiz.mistake: Works out perimeter (70) or adds the sides (35)

quiz.q: A square carrom board has side 70 cm. What is its area?
quiz.explain: Area of a square = side × side = 70 × 70 = 4900 cm².
quiz.mistake: Finds perimeter (280), doubles the side (140), or drops a zero (490)

quiz.q: A rectangle is made of 5 rows of unit squares with 7 squares in each row. What is its area?
quiz.explain: 5 rows of 7 squares = 5 × 7 = 35 unit squares.
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 + 7 (12) or finds the perimeter (24)

quiz.q: A room floor is 6 m by 4 m. Tiles of 1 m × 1 m cost ₹50 each. How much does it cost to tile the floor?
quiz.explain: The floor needs 6 × 4 = 24 tiles. 24 × ₹50 = ₹1200.
quiz.mistake: Uses the perimeter, 20 m (₹1000), instead of the area

quiz.q: A rectangle has area 48 cm² and breadth 6 cm. What is its length?
quiz.explain: Length × 6 = 48, so length = 48 ÷ 6 = 8 cm.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts instead of dividing (42)

quiz.q: Rectangle A is 6 cm × 4 cm. Rectangle B is 8 cm × 3 cm. Which is true?
quiz.explain: Both areas are 24 cm². The perimeters are 2 × 10 = 20 cm and 2 × 11 = 22 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal areas must mean equal perimeters

quiz.q: Aisha cuts a 10 cm × 10 cm square of paper into 1 cm × 1 cm squares. How many small squares does she get?
quiz.explain: 10 rows of 10 small squares make 10 × 10 = 100.
quiz.mistake: Counts only around the edge (40) or adds the sides (20)

quiz.q: A square has perimeter 20 cm. What is its area?
quiz.explain: Side = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm, so area = 5 × 5 = 25 cm².
quiz.mistake: Thinks the area equals the perimeter, or squares the perimeter (400)

teach.ask: Gappu wants to cover his nest floor with soft leaves: 'How do I work out the area?'
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! Area is the space inside, length × breadth, in square units. My nest will be so cosy!
teach.nudge: Do I add or multiply the sides? And what units does area use?

learn.hook: Why do we measure area with squares, not circles? Try tiling a floor with round tiles!
points: Squares are the best unit for area: they fit together with no gaps and no overlaps, and they line up neatly in rows and columns.
Circles leave gaps; triangles work too, but squares match length × breadth.
Estimating the area of an irregular shape on squared paper: count full squares as 1, more than half a square as 1, exactly half as ½, and ignore less than half.
Then add them up. The answer is an estimate in square units.

example.q: A leaf on squared paper covers 14 full squares, 6 more-than-half squares, 4 half squares and 5 less-than-half squares. Estimate its area.
steps: Less than half: ignore. Total: 14 + 6 + 2 = 22 square units.

learn.reallife: Map makers estimate the area of lakes and forests by laying a square grid over the map.

games.title: Count as...
items: A full square
Three quarters of a square
Most of a square
Exactly half a square
A square cut corner to corner (half)
A tiny corner
A thin sliver
A quarter of a square

quiz.q: Why are squares used as units of area?
options: They cover a surface with no gaps or overlaps
quiz.explain: Squares tile completely and line up in rows and columns.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any shape works as well

quiz.q: Why are circles poor units for measuring area?
options: They leave gaps when placed together
quiz.explain: Circles cannot cover a surface without gaps.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the gaps

quiz.q: A shape covers 9 full squares, 4 more-than-half squares and 6 less-than-half squares. What is its estimated area?
quiz.explain: 9 + 4 = 13. Less-than-half squares are ignored.
quiz.mistake: Counts the less-than-half squares too

quiz.q: A pond covers 15 full squares and 8 half squares. Estimate its area.
quiz.explain: 8 halves = 4 whole squares. 15 + 4 = 19.
quiz.mistake: Counts each half as 1

quiz.q: A map of a lake has 20 full squares, 6 more-than-half, 4 half and 7 less-than-half squares. What is the estimate?
quiz.mistake: Counts halves as 1 or adds the tiny ones

quiz.q: Which part of a square should be ignored when estimating area?
quiz.explain: Pieces smaller than half are left out.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the counting rules

quiz.q: Rekha traces her palm on 1 cm squared paper: 32 full, 10 more-than-half, 6 half and 9 less-than-half. Estimate her palm's area.
quiz.mistake: Counts the half squares as whole

quiz.q: Each square on a map is 1 km × 1 km. A forest covers about 12 squares. What is its approximate area?
quiz.explain: 12 squares of 1 square km each is about 12 square km (12 km²). Area uses square units.
quiz.mistake: Writes the area in km instead of km²

teach.ask: Gappu put his feather on squared paper. 'Do I count the tiny bits of squares too?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Ignore the tiny bits, count more-than-half as 1 and exact halves as half!
teach.nudge: What do we do with pieces less than half a square?

learn.hook: Seven pieces, one square, a thousand pictures! And every picture has the same area.
points: A tangram cuts a square into 7 pieces: 2 large triangles, 1 medium triangle, 2 small triangles, 1 square and 1 parallelogram.
If the whole tangram is 16 square units: each large triangle is 4, the medium triangle 2, each small triangle 1, the square 2 and the parallelogram 2.
So the square, the parallelogram and the medium triangle each equal 2 small triangles, and a large triangle equals 2 medium triangles. Their perimeters, though, are not all equal.
Rectangles with the same area can have different perimeters. Area 24 cm²: 1 × 24 (P = 50), 2 × 12 (P = 28), 3 × 8 (P = 22), 4 × 6 (P = 20).

example.q: Using whole-number sides, which rectangle of area 36 cm² has the smallest perimeter?
steps: The 6 × 6 square has the smallest perimeter, 24 cm.

learn.reallife: Farmers with a fixed amount of land (area) choose shapes that need less fencing (perimeter).

games.title: Tangram facts (whole square = 16 units)
items: A large triangle has area 4 units.
It is a quarter of the whole.
The square piece and the parallelogram have equal areas.
Each is 2 units.
A small triangle has area 2 units.
It is 1 unit.
Two small triangles make the same area as the medium triangle.
All 7 pieces together make 16 units.

quiz.q: A tangram square has area 64 cm². What is the area of one large triangle?
quiz.explain: Each large triangle is a quarter of the square: 64 ÷ 4 = 16 cm².
quiz.mistake: Thinks a large triangle is half the square

quiz.q: In that 64 cm² tangram, what is the area of one small triangle?
quiz.explain: A small triangle is 1/16 of the square: 64 ÷ 16 = 4 cm².
quiz.mistake: Uses one-eighth

quiz.q: Which tangram piece has the same area as the medium triangle?
quiz.explain: The square, the parallelogram and the medium triangle each equal two small triangles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks different shapes must have different areas

quiz.q: How many small tangram triangles make up the area of one large triangle?
quiz.explain: Large = 4 units, small = 1 unit, so 4 small triangles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is 2

quiz.q: Which rectangle of area 24 cm² has the largest perimeter?
quiz.explain: 1 × 24 gives 2 × 25 = 50 cm, the largest.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the same area means the same perimeter

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a 3 cm × 8 cm rectangle?
quiz.mistake: Gives the area (24) instead

quiz.q: Two rectangles both have area 18 cm²: 2 × 9 and 3 × 6. How much bigger is the first one's perimeter?
quiz.explain: 2 × 9: 22 cm. 3 × 6: 18 cm. Difference 4 cm.
quiz.mistake: Assumes equal areas mean equal perimeters

quiz.q: A farmer has 100 m² of land as a rectangle with whole-number sides. Which shape needs the least fencing?
quiz.explain: 10 × 10 has perimeter 40 m, the smallest of these.
quiz.mistake: Picks a long thin rectangle

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'All my rectangles cover 12 squares. Do they all need the same length of fence?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Same area, different perimeters: the long thin one needs the most fence!
teach.nudge: Compare a 1 × 12 and a 3 × 4 rectangle. Which needs more fence?

topics.title: Area puzzles: triangles and odd shapes

learn.hook: Cut a sandwich corner to corner and each half has exactly half the area. That simple idea solves many puzzles!
points: A diagonal cuts a rectangle into two equal triangles, so each triangle has half the rectangle's area.
For shapes made of rectangles (like an L shape), split them into rectangles, find each area and add.
On a grid, count full squares as 1 and two half squares as 1 more.
Cutting a shape and rearranging the pieces without overlap keeps the same area. This is the idea behind the tangram.
To find an area with a hole, find the whole area and subtract the hole.

example.q: An L shape is made of a 6 cm × 2 cm rectangle and a 2 cm × 3 cm rectangle. Find its area.

learn.reallife: Working out paint for an L-shaped room or cloth for a triangular flag uses these tricks.

games.title: Match the shape to its area
pairs: Half of a 6 cm × 4 cm rectangle
Half of a 10 cm × 3 cm rectangle
A 3 cm × 5 cm and a 2 cm × 2 cm rectangle joined
8 full grid squares and 4 half squares
One half of a 4 cm square cut along a diagonal

games.title: Area puzzle facts
items: A diagonal cuts a rectangle into two triangles of equal area.
The two triangles fit exactly on top of each other.
If you cut a shape and rearrange the pieces without overlapping, the area stays the same.
No paper is added or lost.
A shape with a bigger perimeter always has a bigger area.
A 1 cm × 9 cm rectangle has perimeter 20 cm but area 9 cm², less than a 4 cm × 4 cm square (perimeter 16 cm, area 16 cm²).
Two half squares on a grid together make 1 square unit.
Half + half = 1.
A triangle cut from a 4 cm × 6 cm rectangle along its diagonal has area 24 cm².
It has half the area: 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm².

quiz.q: A rectangular sheet 8 cm × 6 cm is cut along a diagonal. What is the area of each triangle?
quiz.explain: The rectangle's area is 8 × 6 = 48 cm². Each triangle is half: 24 cm².
quiz.mistake: Forgets to halve (48) or halves twice (12)

quiz.q: An L-shaped room is made of a 5 m × 4 m part and a 3 m × 2 m part. What is its total area?
quiz.explain: 5 × 4 = 20 m² and 3 × 2 = 6 m². Together: 26 m².
quiz.mistake: Adds all the lengths (14) or counts only one part (20)

quiz.q: On a grid, a leaf covers 9 full squares and 6 half squares. What is its area?
quiz.explain: 6 half squares make 3 full squares. 9 + 3 = 12 square units.
quiz.mistake: Counts each half square as a whole square (15)

quiz.q: A square garden 10 m × 10 m has a square pond of side 2 m in it. What area is left for grass?
quiz.explain: Garden: 10 × 10 = 100 m². Pond: 2 × 2 = 4 m². Grass: 100 − 4 = 96 m².
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the pond's perimeter (8) instead of its area

quiz.q: A tangram square has area 16 cm². Riya uses all its pieces, without overlapping, to make a cat. What is the cat's area?
quiz.explain: Rearranging the same pieces does not change the area, so the cat is 16 cm².
quiz.mistake: Thinks a new shape must have a new area

quiz.q: A 2 cm × 2 cm square is cut out from the corner of a 12 cm × 5 cm rectangle. What is the area of what is left?
quiz.explain: 12 × 5 = 60 cm². The cut-out is 2 × 2 = 4 cm². 60 − 4 = 56 cm².
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract the cut-out (60) or adds it (64)

quiz.q: Two triangles, each half of a 4 cm × 3 cm rectangle, are put together. What is their total area?
quiz.explain: Two halves make the whole rectangle: 4 × 3 = 12 cm².
quiz.mistake: Gives the area of only one triangle (6)

quiz.q: Joseph's T-shaped kite is made of a 6 cm × 2 cm top bar and a 2 cm × 5 cm stem. What is its area?
quiz.explain: Top bar: 6 × 2 = 12 cm². Stem: 2 × 5 = 10 cm². Total: 22 cm².
quiz.mistake: Adds all the lengths (15) or multiplies everything together (120)

teach.ask: Gappu has an L-shaped leaf: 'It's not a rectangle! How do I find its area?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Cut it into rectangles, find each area and add them up. Easy peasy!
teach.nudge: Can I break the shape into simpler pieces first? What do I do after that?

learn.hook: Draw any triangle inside a rectangle on the same base, touching the top side. Its area is always half. Always!
points: If a triangle has the same base as a rectangle and its top corner touches the opposite side, its area is half the rectangle's area.
Why: a line from the top corner straight down splits the rectangle into two smaller rectangles. The triangle takes half of each.
So a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm has area half of 10 × 6 = 30 cm².
To find the area of odd shapes, split them into rectangles and triangles, find each area, and add.

example.q: A shape is a 6 cm × 4 cm rectangle with a triangle on top whose base is 6 cm and height 2 cm. Find the total area.

learn.reallife: A house front wall with a triangular roof part is a rectangle plus a triangle, so painters find its area this way.

items.q: Rectangle 5 by 4 plus a triangle of base 5, height 2

games.title: Triangle and rectangle
items: A triangle on the same base touching the top side has half the rectangle's area.
It takes half of each part.
Moving the top corner along the top side changes the area.
The base and height stay the same.
A triangle of base 8 cm and height 3 cm has area 24 cm².
It is half of 24: 12 cm².
We can split odd shapes into rectangles and triangles.
Then add the areas.
A diagonal splits a rectangle into two equal triangles.
Each is half.

quiz.q: A triangle sits inside a 12 cm × 8 cm rectangle on its 12 cm base, with its top corner on the opposite side. What is its area?
quiz.explain: Half of 12 × 8 = 48 cm².
quiz.mistake: Gives the whole rectangle's area

quiz.q: The top corner of that triangle slides along the top side. What happens to the area?
quiz.explain: The base (12 cm) and height (8 cm) don't change, so the area stays half the rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a slanted triangle is smaller

quiz.q: A triangular flag has base 30 cm and height 20 cm. What is its area?
quiz.explain: Half of 30 × 20 = 300 cm².
quiz.mistake: Forgets to halve

quiz.q: A house wall is an 8 m × 5 m rectangle with a triangular top of base 8 m and height 3 m. What is the total area?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to halve the triangle

quiz.q: A 10 cm × 6 cm rectangle has a triangle cut out of it, with base 10 cm and height 6 cm. What area is left?
quiz.explain: The triangle is half, so half (30 cm²) is left.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the full rectangle

quiz.q: Why is a triangle on the same base and height as a rectangle exactly half of it?
options: A line down from its top corner splits the rectangle into two parts, and the triangle is half of each
quiz.explain: Each smaller rectangle is cut in half by a side of the triangle.
quiz.mistake: Cannot explain why

quiz.q: A shape is made of a 4 cm × 4 cm square and a triangle of base 4 cm and height 4 cm on one side. What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Counts the triangle as a full square

quiz.q: A right-angled triangle has the two short sides 9 cm and 4 cm. What is its area?
quiz.explain: It is half of a 9 × 4 rectangle: 18 cm².
quiz.mistake: Adds the sides

teach.ask: Gappu draws a pointy triangle inside his 6 × 4 nest-mat, on the 6 side, tip touching the top. 'What is its area?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Half of 6 × 4, so 12 square units, wherever the tip is!
teach.nudge: How does the triangle compare to the rectangle around it?

learn.hook: Twelve square tiles: make a long snake or a neat block. Which needs less border?
points: With the same number of unit squares (same area), a compact shape like a square or near-square has the smallest perimeter; a long line has the largest.
12 unit squares: a 3 × 4 rectangle has perimeter 14 units; a 1 × 12 line has 26 units.
Adding one square to a figure can increase the perimeter (touching 1 side: +2), keep it the same (touching 2 sides: 0) or decrease it (touching 3 sides: −2).
Shapes with the same perimeter can have different areas: perimeter 20 cm can be 5 × 5 = 25 cm² or 9 × 1 = 9 cm². And same area can have different perimeters.

example.q: A square is added to a figure so that it touches the figure along exactly 2 of its sides. What happens to the perimeter?
steps: 2 of its sides are joined to the figure, hiding 2 old edges.
2 new edges are added and 2 old edges disappear: no change.

learn.reallife: Arranging tables for a party: pushing tables into a block uses less tablecloth edging than a long line.

games.title: Adding a square: perimeter goes...
items: New square touches 1 side
Square stuck on the end of a line
Square fills an L-shaped corner
New square touches 2 sides
Square fills a notch touching 3 sides
New square touches 3 sides

quiz.q: With 18 unit squares, which arrangement has the smallest perimeter?
quiz.mistake: Thinks same area means same perimeter

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of 10 unit squares placed in a single line?
quiz.explain: A 1 × 10 rectangle: 2 × (10 + 1) = 22 units.
quiz.mistake: Counts 2 per square

quiz.q: A figure has perimeter 16 units. A new square is added touching it along just 1 side. What is the new perimeter?
quiz.explain: The new square adds 3 edges and hides 1: +2. 16 + 2 = 18.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 for the new square

quiz.q: A figure has perimeter 20 units. A square is placed in a notch where it touches 3 sides. What is the new perimeter?
quiz.explain: It adds 1 edge and hides 3: −2. 20 − 2 = 18.
quiz.mistake: Thinks adding a square always increases the perimeter

quiz.q: Two rectangles both have perimeter 24 cm: 6 cm × 6 cm and 10 cm × 2 cm. What are their areas?
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal perimeters mean equal areas

quiz.q: Which has a larger area: a 7 × 3 rectangle or a 5 × 5 square? (Both have perimeter 20.)
quiz.mistake: Assumes same perimeter means same area

quiz.q: Sana arranges 9 unit squares. What is the largest perimeter she can make (squares joined edge to edge)?
quiz.explain: A straight line 1 × 9: 2 × (9 + 1) = 20 units.
quiz.mistake: Uses 4 × 9 for separate squares

quiz.q: What is the smallest perimeter for 9 unit squares joined edge to edge?
quiz.explain: A 3 × 3 square: 4 × 3 = 12 units.
quiz.mistake: Picks a long shape

teach.ask: Gappu has 16 square crackers. 'How do I arrange them so the border is as short as possible?'
teach.praise: Chirp! A 4 by 4 square: perimeter 16. Much shorter than a line of 34!
teach.nudge: Should the shape be long and thin, or close to a square?

learn.hook: Be an architect: find the missing lengths on a house plan, then crack an area maze!
points: On a house plan, lengths along one wall add up: if the house is 12 m wide and the bedroom is 5 m wide, the room next to it is 12 − 5 = 7 m wide.
Room area = length × width of that room. Add rooms for the total.
Area maze: a rectangle is split into parts with some areas and lengths given. Use area ÷ known side = missing side, then carry that length to the next part.
Drawing to order: a rectangle with area 16 cm² and perimeter 16 cm is 4 × 4. Inside an 8 × 6 rectangle (48 cm²), a 4 × 6 rectangle has half the area.

example.q: A rectangle is split into two parts side by side, both 6 cm tall. The left part has area 24 cm² and the right part 18 cm². How wide is the whole rectangle?

learn.reallife: Architects and builders read plans to order the right number of tiles for each room.

items.text: House 15 m wide, room 6 m → other room ___ m

quiz.q: A house is 14 m long. The kitchen takes 5 m of that length and the hall takes the rest. How long is the hall?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting

quiz.q: That hall is 9 m long and 4 m wide. What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Gives the perimeter's half (13)

quiz.q: A plan shows a bedroom 4 m × 3 m and a study 3 m × 3 m. What is their total area?
quiz.mistake: Adds the sides

quiz.q: Area maze: the left part has area 24 cm² and height 4 cm. The right part shares the height and has area 20 cm². How wide is the right part?
quiz.explain: Shared height 4 cm. Right width = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the left part's width

quiz.q: In that maze (left 24 cm², right 20 cm², height 4 cm), how wide is the whole rectangle?
quiz.explain: Left width 24 ÷ 4 = 6, right width 5. Total 6 + 5 = 11 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds the areas instead of widths

quiz.q: Which rectangle has area 16 cm² and perimeter 20 cm?
quiz.mistake: Checks only the area

quiz.q: A rectangle is 10 cm × 6 cm. Which rectangle drawn inside it has exactly half its area?
quiz.explain: Half of 60 is 30, and 5 × 6 = 30.
quiz.mistake: Halves both sides (giving a quarter)

quiz.q: A square room has area 25 m². A rug 3 m × 4 m is laid on it. How much floor is left uncovered?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the rug's perimeter

teach.ask: Gappu's plan: the nest is 10 cm wide, the left room is 4 cm wide. 'How wide is the right room?'
teach.praise: Tweet! 10 − 4 = 6 cm. Plans are just careful subtraction!
teach.nudge: What do the two room widths add up to?
